record.original_question: Prove that the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation is non-integrable under at least one reasonable notion of infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian integrability.

evidence.quote: Problem 26. Prove the non-integrability of the 2D Euler equation. It is worth to emphasize that, while there is a number of papers related to infinitely many conserved quantities or the Lax form of the Euler equation in 2D (see, e.g., [47, 85]), these features cannot be regarded as good indicators of integrability. The existence of a Lax pair is a property of all Euler–Poincaré equations, since the latter are Hamiltonian on the dual space to a Lie algebra with respect to the Lie–Poisson structure and hence are given by the coadjoint operator, “mimicking the commutator” in the Lie algebra. Typically, in order to prove algebraic- geometric integrability of a Lax equation one needs to present a Lax form nontrivially depending on a spectral parameter. However, no such form has been found for the 2D Euler equations. On the other hand, one could try to prove non-integrability of this infinite-dimensional system with the help of the methods used to show non-integrability of finite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems. This could invoke, for instance, the methods related to nontrivial monodromies for periodic orbits [153, 109], or Melnikov integrals for bifurcations of saddle separatrices, or one might be able to proceed by means of a “local” analysis in the vicinity of a steady solution. Since there are several (not necessarily equivalent) definitions of integrability in infinite dimensions, the above problem would be to show that the 2D Euler equations fail to satisfy at least one of these integrability definitions. Note that the set of all Casimirs has been recently fully described in [58, 61] for two-dimensional surfaces M without boundary for the groups of symplectic and Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms. The two-dimensional boundary case was settled in [78].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation for an ideal fluid on a surface $M$ (for concreteness, take $M$ to be the two-torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ or the two-sphere $S^2$), written in vorticity form as
$$\partial_t \omega + \{\psi, \omega\} = 0, \qquad \omega = \Delta \psi,$$
where $\omega: M \to \mathbb{R}$ is the vorticity, $\psi$ is the stream function, $\Delta$ is the Laplace–Beltrami operator, and $\{f,g\} = \partial_x f\,\partial_y g - \partial_y f\,\partial_x g$ is the canonical Poisson bracket on $M$. This system is an infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian system on the dual of the Lie algebra $\mathrm{SVect}(M)$ of divergence-free vector fields on $M$, equipped with the Lie–Poisson structure, and its Hamiltonian is the kinetic energy $H(\omega) = \tfrac12 \int_M |\nabla \psi|^2$.

Although the system possesses an infinite family of Casimir invariants (the moments $\int_M f(\omega)\,d\mu$ for any smooth $f$) and admits a formal Lax representation arising automatically from its Euler–Poincaré structure, no Lax pair depending nontrivially on a spectral parameter is known, and the existence of such a representation (or of action–angle coordinates) is not established.

Problem. Formulate a precise reasonable notion of integrability for infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems—for instance, one of:
(a) algebraic-geometric integrability arising from a Lax pair with a nontrivial spectral parameter;
(b) the existence of a complete set of functionally independent Poisson-commuting first integrals giving an invariant foliation by Lagrangian tori in a suitable functional-analytic sense;
(c) integrability in the sense of meromorphic/real-analytic first integrals along a generic invariant submanifold (in the spirit of Ziglin–Morales-Ramis or Melnikov-type obstructions applied to periodic orbits and saddle separatrices of the Euler flow)—

and prove that the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation is not integrable in that sense. Equivalently, exhibit a rigorous obstruction (e.g. nontrivial monodromy of variational equations along a periodic solution, a nonvanishing Melnikov integral for a heteroclinic/homoclinic connection of stationary solutions, or a differential-Galois obstruction) that rules out integrability of the 2D Euler equation.
artifact.status_search_result: The non-integrability of the 2D Euler equation is a long-standing open problem. While 2D Euler admits infinitely many Casimir invariants and a formal Lax representation coming from its Euler–Poincaré/Lie–Poisson structure, no spectral-parameter Lax pair is known, and no rigorous proof of non-integrability under any standard infinite-dimensional notion has been published. The problem is listed as open in recent problem collections on hydrodynamics and Hamiltonian PDEs.
